## Diabetes visualizations

- #1 First we call the data and assign the names accurately in order to be able to compare. 
- #2 Make the income column numeric
- #3 Test out different regression models to see what represents our data. Linear doesn't work for our model, must check other regressions
- #4 Test out quadratic regression. Looks like a match!
- #5 Lastly, create a scatter plot with a quadratic regression line to visualize the data and be able to analyze results

```{r}
#1
new_data <- read.csv("cleaned_county_data.csv")
diabetes_data <- new_data %>% 
  filter(MeasureId == "DIABETES")

#2
diabetes_data$Median_Household_Income = as.numeric(diabetes_data$Median_Household_Income)

#3
model <- lm(Data_Value ~ Median_Household_Income, data = diabetes_data)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)

#4
model2 <- lm(
  Data_Value ~ Median_Household_Income +
    I(Median_Household_Income^2),
  data = diabetes_data
  )
summary(model2)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model2)

#5
ggplot(diabetes_data, aes(x = Median_Household_Income, y = Data_Value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x + I(x^2), color = "darkred", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "County Median Household Income vs. Diabetes Prevalence",
    subtitle = "CDC PLACES & US Census ACS Data",
    x = "Median Household Income ($)",
    y = "Diabetes Prevalence (%)"
  )

```

## Preliminary visualizations for Depression data

- #1 Since we found our diabetes data to be quadratic, we assumed that our depression data would be quadratic aswell. We made a graph with this assumption in mind. We made a new set comparing Measure Id's of Depression in comparison to median household income. Our observations of quadratic relationship held true, no other regression models needed.

```{r}
#1
depression_plot <- new_data %>% 
  mutate(Median_Household_Income = as.numeric(as.character(Median_Household_Income))) %>%
  filter(MeasureId == "DEPRESSION") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Median_Household_Income, y = Data_Value)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "darkorchid") + 
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x + I(x^2),
    color = "darkred",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs( 
    title = "Depression Prevalence vs. Median Household Income", 
    subtitle = "CDC PLACES & US Census ACS Data",
    x = "Median Household Income ($)", 
    y = "Depression Prevalence (%)" 
  )

print(depression_plot)

```

We have all the data cleaned, processed, and visualized. Now we can analyze our results and make sense of what they mean.
